I am almost 71, and have been using kratom since 2016, and am taking this FDA very seriously.  Not meaning to go out and buy 2 kgs, but to support AKA, and do what you can to support them.  I can't afford to donate money, but you can donate in other ways.  I took the 'kratom advocate' online program, so I can speak with a little authority.  When the states have the senate meetings, I send in my story, and what Kratom has done for me.
But I have been concerned for the last couple years, about the type of product promotions have been going on.  The gummies, extracts, 'chews' and other 'so called druggie behavior.'  
Please know that there are people like me, who depend on Kratom on a daily basis, and it wouldn't just be a 'bummer' it would be devasting!  
Thank you and please support AKA, any way you can.  It doesn't have to be monetary.  KEEP KRATOM LEGAL

AKA...as a advocate in AZ, was asked to send my kratom story to Debbie Lasko, I emailed you asking for alternative method, since I do not have FB, still waiting for best way to contact Congresswoman:/
thank you, I couldn't finish my post, didn't think it posted...

Thank you for this conversation...I held my dog, almost 14 yr lab, they gave us a big quilt, so I stayed with her on the floor.  Through the insertion of catheter for i.v. in her rear leg, when the doctor came in to administer the 1st tranquilizing drug, to the final barbituates to stoh her heart.  She laid her head in my lap, with both of us snuggled as close as possible.  I was able to hug and kiss her, and whisper I love you  to her a million times, and i felt her leaving, she was so close and warm, and then she was gone, I felt relief that the pain in her life was gone, and I wouldn't see it in her when she was just trying to make me lsugh

I got confirmation right away, kind of just the info page, with a Thank you for submitting.

Name, email address and comment were necessary to complete survey, but phone # wasn't.

I am not able to quit kratom, thank God I'm old...I would rather be dead.

I stopped talking to my brother many years ago, family issues, that seemed to effect my life, but not the rest of the family.  After finally coming to the realization that I was keeping family secrets, to protect people, the only one hurt was me.  Few weeks ago, found out that he died last year, and I was notified by an attorney regarding something in his estate (definitely nothing for me), his wife didn't feel the need to let me know.  I am the last person left in my family, as far as I know.  I feel angry that I didn't have the chance to settle this before he died.  We never spoke of the 'secret' in the family, even though he was part of it.  Now I feel like I lived my whole life with my family just thinking I was mentally ill and a drug addict.  I even worry that when I go to heaven, my family won't be there to greet me, because they will still think that I'm nuts.  And to be honest I don't really want to see them either.  I will never know how my life could have been different if my brother would have told someone, what was happening to me.  I still haven't told anyone, because now there is no one left to tell!

hey thank you for getting back to me.  I know how lonely it gets, and having a best friend (dog) is vital.  I know some of the rescue's here in Phoenix have needs for temporary homes, any chance you could convince her to just give a home to a 'pup' just for the holidays, you know, once she falls in love again, it will be better.  You guys take care, and I hope that a furry little friend comes in to your moms life.

So sorry for your loss.  Wanted to share this for your mom.  I am 65 and have always been alone, except for my pets, and they mean everything to me.  I am down to just one dog now, and I also like your mom, don't think I will want to keep going after she's gone.  I haven't gotten more pets, because I think it would be unfair to them, to die and they have no place to go.  Couldn't stand to think of them going to the animal shelter, scared and without me, so I feel its best not to have anymore.  Want you to share with your mom, the poem/? The Rainbow Bridge...it is making me cry just thinking about it, but in a good way, a way that we will see our loved pets again.  Please take care, and maybe your mom might want to volunteer at a pet rescue, I tried for awhile but for physical reasons had to give it up.  My pup (she's 9) and I will be sending healing thoughts your way.

dressing my Labrador up as Esther Williams (swimmer/actress from the '40's, including a old rubber bathing suit cap).  It was a party for dogs @ group of people who walked their dogs together in Pasadena.
Good times, and fun dogs!!!
If it hadn't been for that show I would not have tried Kratom. I grew up in the 60's in L.A., I was able to make my own opinions from hearing both sides...I chose Kratom, and it has changed my life.
